title: Holding More Than One Travel Protection Plans Certificate
content:
A traveller may hold more than one Travel Protection Plans policy at a time, most often an annual multi-trip plan alongside a single-trip plan bought for an expensive journey. No ceiling is set on the number of policies one traveller may hold.

Two policies never pay the same loss twice. Where both cover one incident, the policy with the earlier issue date pays first and the later policy pays only the balance the first did not reach.

Two single-trip policies covering the same journey are never both issued. The second is declined at quotation, and the traveller is offered an upgrade of the first instead.

A policy covers the travellers named on its certificate and nobody else. A traveller named on two certificates is still one insured person for the purpose of any per-traveller limit.

## The same rules stated as a matter of identity

| What is being asked about | What the rule fixes |
| --- | --- |
| How many certificates one traveller may hold | More than one, with no stated ceiling |
| Which certificate answers an incident both cover | The one with the earlier issue date, first; the later one for the balance only |
| A second single-trip certificate for a journey already insured | Not issued; declined at quotation, with an upgrade of the first offered |
| Who is insured | The travellers named on the certificate, and nobody else |
| A traveller named on two certificates | Still one insured person for any per-traveller limit |

## A holding read through

Take, hypothetically, a traveller holding an Annual Multi-Trip Traveller policy issued in March and a TripGuard Premier policy issued in July for a costly journey. Both are validly held, because the range permits an annual plan alongside a single-trip plan. Should one incident fall within both, the March policy pays first because its issue date is the earlier, and the July policy answers only what the March one did not reach. Were the traveller instead to ask in July for a second single-trip policy over a journey a single-trip policy already insures, that second policy is not issued; the answer at quotation is a declined quotation and the offer of an upgrade to the policy already held.

Because a traveller named on both certificates counts once, a per-traveller limit is not doubled by the second naming; it is the same insured person appearing twice.
